llm.summary: October CPI printed hot — core above forecast — and it has effectively cemented a December Fed rate HIKE, with Waller explicitly saying rates need to go up and Goldman floating hikes running into 2027. The equity market's response was the tell: the Dow still ripped 1,132 points with Amazon and Tesla leading while Nvidia dived, so this is not a broad risk-off, it is a violent rotation out of the single most crowded trade and into cash-flow value, cyclicals and defensives. Brent broke below $90 for the first time since August as Trump backed off striking Iran, which is a genuine disinflationary offset and a direct margin gift to DAL and FDX, but it did not save gold, which fell 2% as real rates repriced. The AI story has split cleanly in two: the physical layer is validated — Constellation +10% on a guidance hike that kills the data-center-moratorium panic, Sanmina +20%, AMAT gapping, Meta funding seven gas plants, X-energy/Dow winning a Texas nuclear permit, gas-plant build costs +66% per BNEF — while the narrative layer takes governance and political damage from the Huang/alleged-Chinese-spy affair, now a class-action suit, a House select committee demand, and per Reuters a likely trigger for tighter chip export law. Anthropic set an IPO range of $70–78 for a $1.3–1.4tn valuation trading Nov 19, which both confirms the capex cycle and introduces an enormous new claim on AI-dedicated capital ahead of SpaceX's own record listing. Sector flows corroborate the rotation: Health Care 96, Staples 93, Real Estate 88, Materials 81 versus Technology at -84 and Comm Services at -25, though Value's lead over Growth narrowed from 140 to 121 points. The regime has hardened into a two-horse race between Reflation (32.9, +10.4) and Stagflation (32.6, +12.7) with Goldilocks collapsing to 17.3 — a hiking Fed into a still-expanding economy. Note the calendar: equities trade today but the Treasury market is closed for Veterans Day, so price action is thin and the bond signal is absent.

market_thesis.short_term: Index level neutral, internals violently rotational. A confirmed December hike plus a hot core print removes the easing option that long-duration growth multiples are priced on, while $89 Brent caps the headline inflation impulse and funds a cyclical/defensive bid. The Nvidia governance and export-control overhang keeps the AI narrative layer de-grossing (Tech flows -84) even as its physical suppliers — CEG, AMAT, SANM, POWL, Broadcom back above $1.5tn — re-rate on contracted cash flow. Expect continued pain in gold, bitcoin (sub-$80k risk), housing-linked names and anything priced off 2027 rate cuts, and continued strength in insurers, healthcare distribution, staples and oil-cost-short transports. Today is low-liquidity with the bond market shut, so moves exaggerate; the Anthropic book-build into Nov 19 is the real liquidity event of the next two weeks.
market_thesis.medium_term: Reflation and Stagflation are now tied at ~33 each with Goldilocks gutted — the market has to price a central bank tightening into an economy that is not breaking. That means higher-for-longer nominal yields, a firmer dollar, compressed multiples on duration, and sustained capital rotation into Health Care, Staples, Real Estate, Materials and Financials. Inside AI, the bifurcation sharpens from 'chips vs. everything' to 'electrons, permits and contracted hardware vs. storytelling and credit'; the 66% jump in gas-plant construction cost and Meta self-funding seven gas plants tell you power is the scarce input and its price is going up, which is itself inflationary and self-reinforcing. Two mega-IPOs (Anthropic ~$1.4tn, SpaceX) will force index and passive reconstitution and drain incremental capital from incumbent AI holdings — the index impact is the underrated risk to the existing megacap complex. The US-China truce extended to 2027 reduces tariff tail risk but the Huang affair guarantees chip export policy tightens, structurally capping the China revenue line for US semis.
market_thesis.long_term: Power, permits and political consent remain the binding constraints on AI, and today's evidence — a historic SMR permit for X-energy/Dow, the Senate advancing a bipartisan critical-infrastructure permitting bill, Venture Global pivoting to off-grid power for data centers, rising public search on 'ai data center water usage' and 'ai data center near me' — maps the decade: generation, grid hardware, copper, gas and nuclear capture durable economics while fabless narrative capture is political and contestable. AI leadership is now a national-security variable, which permanently raises the risk premium on China-exposed semis and embeds duplicated, higher-cost supply chains and a higher inflation floor. Wall Street is simultaneously becoming the world's venue — Dangote scrapping London, the FT writing about index impact of private giants going public — concentrating global capital and index risk in US listings. For households, affordability (electricity, groceries, housing, retirement, healthcare premiums) is the dominant structural variable, entrenching value retail, generics/distribution, insurance, and experiences over undifferentiated discretionary.

short_term: Households absorbing a hot October CPI are trading down — news outlets are literally publishing grocery-cost calculators, which is the behavioural tell for value retail share gain (Walmart upgraded ahead of earnings, DG/DLTR/TGT in the mention tape).
Gasoline relief from sub-$90 Brent transfers a few dollars a week to discretionary spend, and the pattern of the last two years says it goes to experiences and travel before goods.

Savers are re-anchoring on a Fed that is HIKING, not cutting: cash and short-duration yields stay attractive, which suppresses marginal demand for gold (down 2%) and bitcoin (testing the $75-80k band).

Retail and institutional investors are queueing for AI exposure via primary issuance rather than secondary megacaps — Anthropic at $70-78 and SpaceX next is a redirection of the same dollars away from NVDA.
Would-be homebuyers are standing down because a December hike kills the lower-mortgage-rate hope; search interest concentrates on 'housing market crash' rather than purchase intent.

Security anxiety is being monetised: rising queries for 'data breach settlement' and 'data breach lawsuit payout per person', Iran-attributed attacks on French supermarket refrigeration, and a second hack at Nvidia-backed Fireworks AI push cyber spend to the top of the flow stack.

Communities are organising against data centers — the rising query set around water usage and proximity is the leading indicator of siting friction and the reason off-grid/behind-the-meter power deals are proliferating.
Retirement anxiety is surfacing in mainstream finance coverage (Social Security solvency, 'I want my husband to retire at 65'), which supports annuity/insurance demand and defensive income.
long_term: Electricity price becomes a consumer-political variable, not an engineering one: the Czech state taking powers against high power prices, and gas-plant build costs +66%, mark the start of a decade where power bills drive policy and where behind-the-meter generation becomes a competitive advantage for both firms and households.

Security and surveillance shift from service to product — Ring launching a flying drone and ground robot to patrol homes and businesses means consumers will buy autonomous physical security the way they bought cameras.

Knowledge and productivity get rented from AI rather than hired: an Anthropic listing at $1.4tn institutionalises a subscription on cognition, and universities building NVIDIA 'AI factories' makes AI fluency a baseline credential.
Mobility demand persists but shifts to experience over ownership — airlines and travel absorb spend that doesn't go to homes people can't afford to move into.
Home becomes an illiquid asset to improve rather than trade, sustaining repair/remodel demand (MAS) even while transaction volumes stay frozen.

Health spending migrates toward continuous monitoring and metabolic management, but the consumer-telehealth channel (HIMS -11.8%) proves fragile to marketing-spend discipline; durable value accrues to devices, distribution and payers.
Energy security is redefined as electron security: LNG and oil matter less to the marginal investor than firm, dispatchable, local megawatts for compute.
Capital formation moves back onshore and on-exchange in the US while other venues lose listings, concentrating global savings in a narrower set of securities and raising systemic index risk.

what_changed_since_yesterday: October CPI came in hotter than forecast with core above expectations — yesterday the market was frozen waiting on it; today a December hike is effectively cemented and Goldman is publicly floating hikes running through 2027.
Equities refused to break: the Dow surged 1,132 points with Amazon and Tesla leading while Nvidia dived, which reframes the story from index risk to concentrated AI-complex risk.

The regime shifted materially — Reflation jumped to 32.9 (+10.4) and now ties Stagflation at 32.6 (+12.7), while Goldilocks collapsed to 17.3 (-13.3) and Contraction fell to 17.2. The market is pricing a tightening Fed into a still-growing economy, not a recession.

Brent broke below $90 for the first time since August after Trump pulled back from the threat to strike Iran — yesterday oil was merely falling on diplomacy hopes, today it is a confirmed level break and a genuine disinflationary offset.
Gold reversed hard, dropping 2% from the $4,100 area it was holding yesterday; real rates have taken control of the hard-asset trade from geopolitics.

Anthropic moved from a vague IPO story to hard terms: $70-78, $1.3-1.4tn valuation, trading Nov 19. Combined with SpaceX, this is now a quantifiable claim on AI-dedicated capital and an index-reconstitution event.

The Nvidia affair escalated from a board investigation to a shareholder class action, a House select committee demand, reporting that $7.5bn of chips reached China, and a Reuters assessment that new export-tightening legislation is likely.

New power-cost data landed: BNEF reports gas-fired plant construction costs up 66%, and X-energy/Dow secured a historic Texas SMR permit — the relative economics just moved toward nuclear and toward existing generation assets.

Small-cap flows turned positive and long-duration Treasury flows are increasing — an unusual pairing with a hiking Fed that suggests some investors are positioning for the hike to be the last one.
